title: One generated brief is the source of truth
body: All machine and repo onboarding surfaces must consume a single deterministic generated brief. Hand-maintained duplicate command lists or executor lists are forbidden because they recreate the drift that caused this failure.

title: Operator and worker executor are different capabilities
body: Any human or interactive agent that can run local commands can operate DontPanic. Only entries backed by real executor implementations in AGENT_REGISTRY can be dispatched as workers.

title: Orchestrate is a teaching gateway
body: The product verb must exist as a CLI command. `dontpanic orchestrate` explains the local workflow when invoked without a dispatchable plan and forwards to dispatch-from-plan when given a plan id or path.

title: Repo onboarding is non-clobbering
body: Onboarding may create missing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files, but must only update content inside marked DontPanic managed blocks when files already exist.

title: Config-home drift must have a fix path
body: Doctor detection alone is insufficient. The plan includes a reconcile command that can migrate non-conflicting legacy ~/.jarvis state into canonical ~/.dontpanic state and refuses ambiguous destructive merges.

title: Unsupported agents are operator-only until implemented
body: The onboarding brief should name unsupported agents such as Grok or Gemini as valid operators but not valid worker executors unless a real executor is registered.

title: Dashboard singleton is part of onboarding quality
body: Multiple orphaned local dashboards make the operator experience confusing. The same plan closes that root cause with a singleton guard and explicit replace behavior.

title: Budget and iteration blockers need productized next actions
body: Quota cooldowns, budget ceilings, admission thresholds, max_iterations state, and no-progress stops must render concise recommended actions and alternatives. The operator or interactive agent should not infer wait-vs-raise-vs-redispatch decisions from raw logs.

title: CLI and dashboard share operational action data
body: Budget/iteration/setup guidance should be typed once and rendered to both CLI output and dashboard action items. Divergent dashboard and terminal advice would recreate the drift this plan is eliminating.

title: Role assignment must be simple and scoped
body: Assigning implementer, auditor, and goal_auditor should not require hand-editing JSON. The CLI and dashboard must list available worker executors, show current effective role sources, require explicit global vs project scope, and refuse operator-only agents as workers.

title: Configuration needs one cockpit
body: DontPanic has many setup surfaces: global/project config, registry, manifest, roles, runtime evidence, gates, protected paths, quota caps, calibration, circuit breakers, notifications, dashboard, capabilities, adapters, MCP, environments, secrets/auth, install snapshots, and generated state. Humans and interactive agents need one inventory/setup surface with safe commands and human-required steps.

title: DontPanic can plan its own setup and updates
body: When setup or update work is incomplete, DontPanic should emit ActionChoices or draft a DontPanic plan for the needed configuration work, rather than requiring the interactive agent to infer a plan from scattered docs and logs.

title: Dashboard hints are deduped
body: When human input is needed, CLI and agent-facing output should include the dashboard URL or start command once per response, not once per action item. Items may reference the shared affordance by id.

title: Active runs must reconcile plan drift
body: If a human or interactive agent changes plan files while DontPanic is running from older context, DontPanic must detect the fingerprint change before the next paid call or signoff, classify the drift, refresh or pause, and show one reconciliation action.

title: Dogfood: agents_required masks broken global roles at dispatch
body: dispatch-from-plan dry-run resolved implementer=claude/auditor=codex from plan.agents_required, so the broken ~/.dontpanic/config.json roles.implementer='Grok-Builder' (the original-incident config) never surfaced. F004 must validate roles.* against AGENT_REGISTRY independently of any plan override. Recorded as a medium sufficiency finding against F004.

title: Dogfood: sufficiency gate error points at a non-runnable module
body: plan lock REFUSED with 'run F003 sufficiency auditor first (see sufficiency_auditor.py)', but run_sufficiency_audit has no production CLI entry point and requires an injected dispatch= callable; it is referenced only by itself and tests. All prior plans satisfy the gate via a hand-authored operator-critical-review findings file (0 override.json exist). This discoverability gap is in-spirit for this plan. For this plan the artifact was written as claude-critical-review and operator-accepted.

title: Pre-impl review clean; one paid F001 volley authorized
body: Operator-accepted Claude pre-impl review: all 3 objective-contract journeys and 12 acceptance_signals trace to feature ACs; DAG clean. Operator authorized exactly one live (paid) volley for F001, implementer=claude/auditor=codex, interactive mode (quota_readiness=config_required; caps intentionally skipped for this one-shot dogfood). Pauses at pre_impl gate.

title: Quota config-readiness friction (superseded by D019 on final outcome)
body: Getting to quota_readiness=ok was friction-heavy: (a) quota-caps init is a no-op when the caps file exists; (b) caps covered the wrong windows vs observed signal — readiness needs a cap for each dispatched vendor's observed-signal window; codex rolling_7d had signal but no cap; (c) --mode interactive does NOT bypass the dispatch-from-plan quota pre-check. Resolved legitimately by adding the codex rolling_7d cap at doctor's exact recommended value (717413196 = ~1.25x observed 573930557). NOTE: an earlier draft of this entry wrongly said the run stopped at a claude calibration wall and that config was reverted — that was superseded; see D019 for the actual terminal outcome. Full friction in evidence/dispatch-friction-log.md.

title: F001 dispatched, paused on codex over-budget breaker before any paid call
body: With quota_readiness=ok, dispatch-from-plan F001 --confirm ran: supervisor implicitly cleared pre_impl (status=active), then the admission breaker tripped defer:quota_threshold = 'codex percent_weekly 4610.4% > threshold 70.0%'. Volley PAUSED before iteration 0 — NO paid call made; the one-volley budget is intact. 4610% = codex rolling_5h observed (126385341) / its rolling_5h cap (2741314): codex has genuinely burned ~46x its 5h budget on this machine (rolling_7d observed 573930557 too). This is the trust system working: it refused to dispatch to a vendor that is massively over budget. Clearing requires `approve <plan> defer:quota_threshold`, which overrides a real over-budget signal — left as an explicit operator cost decision, NOT auto-cleared. Live ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json retains the legit codex rolling_7d cap (doctor-recommended value); ~/.dontpanic/config.json left untouched (still Grok-Builder, which D015/F004 covers). No source files modified; only the plan dir is new in the repo.

title: approve(defer) alone does NOT force past budget; dispatch re-evaluates admission
body: CORRECTION of a retracted earlier draft of this entry that wrongly claimed the volley ran. Reality: `dontpanic approve <plan> defer:quota_threshold` cleared the gate, but the subsequent `dispatch-from-plan --confirm` re-computed admission fresh ([admission] class=autonomous quota_over=True), re-tripped the SAME defer:quota_threshold, and PAUSED before iteration 0 again — 0 audit JSONs, no agent_brief.py, F001.passes still false, NO paid call. Lesson: the admission breaker is recomputed at each dispatch from live quota_state, so a prior approve does not stick against a still-over-budget vendor. To actually force past it, dispatch must run with --mode interactive (documented as 'bypass admission gates'), not via approve. Next attempt uses --mode interactive per operator 'force and ignore the budget'.

title: F001 volley ran via --mode interactive (paid); auditor needs_changes; stopped_budget after 1 round
body: VERIFIED against audit JSONs (corrects an inaccurate first draft of this entry that misnamed the findings). Per operator 'force and ignore the budget': dispatch-from-plan F001 --mode interactive --confirm bypassed admission (the ONLY thing that gets past the codex over-budget breaker; plain approve+dispatch does NOT — D020). Real paid calls made. iter0 implementer=claude created scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/agent_brief.py (10874 bytes) + tests/test_f001_agent_brief.py (13 tests, all pass — independently re-run: '13 passed'). auditor=codex (688257 tok in / 12740 out / 1 api_call) verdict=needs_changes, 2 findings: (1) medium/correctness — CANONICAL_WORKFLOW at agent_brief.py:77 renders 'project register -> plan author/lock -> ...' but F001 AC required the literal command terms 'projects add' and 'plan lock'; (2) low/test_coverage — test_f001_agent_brief.py:107 doesn't assert those terms. Both findings are REAL (verified in source) — genuine cross-model-audit value: codex caught claude using prose workflow labels instead of the actual CLI verbs, which is exactly the orchestrate-naming class of bug this whole plan exists to kill. Volley then terminated stopped_budget after 1 round (budget_ceiling guard, distinct from the admission breaker) before a fix iteration; loop_caps.max_iterations=3 not reached. F001 NOT converged: features.json F001.passes still false; fix (use literal 'projects add'/'plan lock' in CANONICAL_WORKFLOW + assert in test) + re-audit remain. agent_brief.py + test are UNTRACKED (not committed). Both the friction case (dispatch-friction-log.md) and a real working cross-model audit are now on record.

title: i0 fix applied + codex re-audit signed_off
body: Applied codex's i0 finding: agent_brief.py CANONICAL_WORKFLOW changed from prose ('project register -> plan author/lock') to literal CLI verbs ('projects add -> plan lock'); test_f001_agent_brief.py adds asserts for 'projects add' and 'plan lock'. 13 tests pass. Re-dispatch: first attempt paused on a latched breaker:budget_ceiling (persistent, distinct from admission defer; --mode interactive does NOT bypass it) — cleared via `approve breaker:budget_ceiling`, then dispatch-from-plan F001 --mode interactive --confirm ran a real paid round (codex 1 api_call). VERIFIED on disk (codex-auditor-F001-i0.json, reused filename, ts 08:09): audit_status=signed_off, 0 findings. Volley now PAUSED at pre_merge (human gate) — correct terminal state. F001 implementation+test complete and cross-model approved. features.json F001.passes still false pending human pre_merge approval + close-out (NOT auto-flipped). agent_brief.py + test_f001_agent_brief.py remain untracked (uncommitted). NOTE: the prior i0 needs_changes audit was overwritten by this signed_off one (same filename) — the supersession is captured here since the JSON no longer shows it.

title: pre_merge cleared; `close --feature` is wrong tool for signed_off (no-op, corrected)
body: Operator cleared pre_merge via `approve ... pre_merge` (remaining gates: none) — that IS done and correct. Then attempted `dontpanic close <plan> --feature F001` to flip F001.passes; it FAILED argparse (close requires --operator-resolved + --reason; that surface is ONLY for operator-resolved stopped_no_progress closeouts, NOT clean signed_off features). NO-OP: F001.passes still false, no signoff-F001.json written, plan still active. (An earlier draft of this entry wrongly claimed the close succeeded and flipped passes — retracted; this is the corrected record.) OPEN QUESTION: for a signed_off feature with pre_merge now cleared, the features.json passes-flip is NOT done by `close`; it is completed by the supervisor finishing the volley (resume) or by an explicit operator flip. Determining the correct path before acting. Note: features.json actually has F001-F009 (9 features), not 6.

title: Active runs must reconcile plan drift
body: If plan files change while DontPanic is running, DontPanic must detect that the active run is operating from a stale plan snapshot, classify the change as additive, context-refresh-required, or blocking policy drift, and either refresh the next worker/auditor context or pause before more paid calls/signoff. Concurrent interactive agents or humans changing the plan must not silently leave another agent executing obsolete instructions.

title: No clean no-paid signed_off -> features.passes finalizer exists; scope into F007
body: Read-only investigation (operator + claude agree): there is NO existing path to flip features.json passes:true for a cleanly auditor-signed_off feature without a paid re-dispatch. Evidence: (1) resume --all/--gate only clears gates, does not continue the volley; (2) dispatch-from-plan re-enters supervisor.dispatch_volley fresh, re-running implementer+auditor (paid); (3) the pre_merge pause happens BEFORE _emit_volley_terminal, so no signoff is written at the pause point; (4) _emit_volley_terminal writes audit/signoff-<plan>.json but does NOT flip features.json; (5) _flip_feature_passes exists only in closeout.py behind close --operator-resolved / no_progress closeout, NOT the clean signed_off path; (6) plan close is plan-level active->completed, wrong per-feature and wrong while F002-F010 pending. Hand-editing features.json would work mechanically but is not a real product path. RECOMMENDATION: productize a clean signed-off feature finalizer under F007 — consume the existing signed_off auditor artifact + cleared gates, write/repair the signoff envelope if missing, flip ONLY that feature's passes:true with evidence_refs, no paid calls. Until that exists, F001 deliverables (agent_brief.py + test, untracked) stay PARKED rather than committing a half-resolved ledger (F001 work signed_off but passes:false).

title: Orchestration frontier is a single deadlocked feature; do not dispatch
body: Asked to run next-best dontpanic across all features. Re-fingerprinted post-amendment (10 features) and ran read-only `dontpanic next`: ready-now = ONLY F001; F002-F010 are a strict blocked chain (F001->F002->...->F010). No fan-out is possible — the DAG is near-linear. F001's code is already implemented + codex signed_off but stuck at passes:false because the no-paid finalizer (D025/F007 AC9-12) does not exist yet. Re-dispatching F001 would re-run implementer+auditor (paid, codex ~46x over budget) and still hit the same no-flip dead end = zero progress. BOOTSTRAP DEADLOCK: the finalizer that would flip F001 lives in F007, which is itself gated behind F001->...->F006, so orchestration cannot reach it. Decision: did NOT dispatch anything (no-progress + paid = wrong). Break-the-deadlock options surfaced to operator: (1) build the F007 finalizer as ordinary out-of-band dev work (TDD), then no-paid finalize F001 to unblock the chain — highest leverage; (2) re-scope DAG so the finalizer has no upstream deps; (3) operator hand-flip F001.passes (rejected as non-real-path per D025 unless explicitly overridden). Minor product bug noted: `dontpanic next` --help prints a massively duplicated usage block, and `next` takes --plan not a positional.

title: Signed_off finalizer shipped out-of-band (TDD); F001 finalized, deadlock broken
body: Built the no-paid signed_off finalizer as ordinary local dev work (NOT dispatched — that would re-hit the D026 bootstrap deadlock). Files: scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/signed_off_finalizer.py (finalize_signed_off_feature + FinalizeError codes not_signed_off/pre_merge_uncleared/no_audit + FinalizeResult), tests/test_signed_off_finalizer.py (9 tests, all green: AC9 success, signoff-no-clobber, 3 refusals + distinct-codes, AC11 idempotency, AC12 monkeypatched dispatch_volley boobytrap proving no paid call), and a `dontpanic finalize <plan> --feature <F>` CLI (exit 0 ok / 3 not_signed_off / 4 pre_merge_uncleared / 5 no_audit). Reuses closeout._flip_feature_passes + signoff_writer.write_signoff + gate_pause.is_gate_cleared — no new executor path. VERIFIED on real F001: `dontpanic finalize ... --feature F001` flipped features.json F001.passes=true (evidence_refs -> audit/signoff-*.json), repaired the missing signoff envelope, zero paid calls; idempotent re-run = no-op. Frontier recomputed: F001 DONE, F002 now READY — the chain is unblocked. Regression sweep 36 passed (finalizer + closeout + lifecycle-gates + agent_brief). NOTE/wart: the evidence_ref note reads 'operator_resolved close-out (class=signed_off_finalize)' because _flip_feature_passes hardcodes that prefix; cosmetic, worth a follow-up to parameterize. SCOPE: F007.passes is NOT flipped — this is one of F007's AC(9)-(12) built+tested out-of-band, but F007 as a whole was never dispatched/audited; its passes:true is an operator decision, not mine to self-certify. agent_brief.py + signed_off_finalizer.py + both test files remain untracked/uncommitted.

title: F002 deployed via dontpanic orchestration — codex signed_off, operator-resolved close on untracked-test backstop
body: Ran live dontpanic dispatch-from-plan on F002 (agent/orchestrate gateway). Cross-model volley: claude implemented agent_surface.py + cli/manifest wiring + 21-test suite; codex audited. Convergence history: run1 needs_changes->stopped_budget; run2 (claude-only) no-op pause; run3 codex backend network failure (blocked, not a judgment); run4 raised codex rolling_5h cap 2.74e6->1e9 in ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json (OPERATOR OVERRIDE, codex was 46x over) + needs_changes x2 -> stopped_no_progress (2 real small findings: agent-status classification, orchestrate bad-flag teaching output); run5 (--max-iterations 5) codex SIGNED_OFF but volley terminated blocked on patch-completeness (untracked test file, D025 root-cause #2). Operator git-add'd deliverables (test 21/21 green) + dontpanic close --operator-resolved --reason evidence_shape_disagreement --allow-missing-breaker. F002.passes=true. FRICTION for follow-up: (1) audit-filename-reuse — re-dispatch with fewer iterations leaves a stale higher-index iN envelope; finalizer/close + memo auto-lift pick it as 'latest' by index not mtime, mislabeling latest_audit_status. (2) codex 46x over quota AND transient backend outage both blocked progress before the budget guard mattered — forcing codex needs both cap-raise AND service health. (3) dispatch-from-plan needs --confirm to actually run (no --mode-only); strict dry-run otherwise.

title: DontPanic bug: no_progress breaker trips on verdict-STRING equality, not finding-set — caps every volley at 2 rounds
body: circuit_breakers.check_no_progress (circuit_breakers.py:938-942) trips when prior_status==current_status with status not in {signed_off,blocked} — i.e. two consecutive 'needs_changes' verdicts, regardless of whether the FINDINGS changed. supervisor.py:2493 calls it with only verdict strings (prior_aud_status, aud_status), never the envelopes. compute_audit_finding_signature exists and is used by check_diminishing_returns (the sibling breaker, correctly compares finding identity per D001/D002) but NOT by check_no_progress. IMPACT: F003 volleys converged on findings (round1 3->round2 i1 had 1 finding; clear movement) but still terminated stopped_no_progress at 2 rounds both times. --max-iterations 8 never reached: no_progress check runs before the iteration-cap check in the loop. So repeated same-recipe dispatch of any feature that takes >2 rounds to converge is STRUCTURALLY incapable of reaching signoff via the volley alone. This is why F002 only landed via operator-resolved close (mechanical block), not a clean signoff terminal. FIX (follow-up plan / harness D-entry): make check_no_progress compare finding signatures across rounds like check_diminishing_returns — pass both auditor envelopes, extract findings, compute_audit_finding_signature, trip only when signature SETS are identical (same findings persist) not when verdict string repeats. Until fixed, multi-round features must be landed via I-fix-then-codex-audit-only or operator-resolved close, NOT repeated volleys.

title: F003 deployed via fix-it-myself + codex audit-only (working path around D029 no_progress bug)
body: F003 (repo_onboarding managed-block writer) volleys kept hitting stopped_no_progress at 2 rounds (D029 bug: trips on verdict-string, not finding-set). Findings genuinely converged: round1 3->round2-i1 1 finding (managed-block in-marker tamper trusts marker hash alone). RESOLUTION: operator fixed the 1 finding directly — _block_is_fresh + _block_is_fresh_bytes now recompute the on-disk body hash and require it to match the stored marker hash (tamper-in-marker -> stale -> rewritten). Added 2 regression tests (test_block_is_fresh_rejects_in_marker_tamper + test_apply_onboarding_rewrites_in_marker_tampered_block); full F003 suite 23 passed. Then `dontpanic <plan> --feature F003 --role auditor` (single-agent audit-only, no volley) -> codex SIGNED_OFF (0 findings, explicitly 'prior tamper-detection issue now returns stale as expected'). Landed: git add deliverables, archived stale codex-auditor-F003-i1.json (needs_changes, superseded) so finalizer picks i0 signed_off (D028 filename-reuse hazard again), signed_off_finalizer flipped passes:true. PATTERN (reusable until D029 fixed): multi-round features -> fix findings by hand + single-agent codex audit-only + finalizer, NOT repeated volleys. Audit-only avoids the 2-round no_progress cap entirely. PROCESS NOTE: accidentally spawned 3 concurrent audit-only runs; stopped 2 via TaskStop. Watch background-dispatch fan-out.

title: F004 deployed via genuine codex cross-model signed_off (i2) + no-paid finalizer
decision: F004 (roles worker-assignment surface) reached passes:true. After the volley false-tripped no_progress twice (D029), I fixed codex's findings by hand: the medium (shlex-quote project paths) and high (untracked files) were already resolved in earlier iterations; the remaining low finding (roles --help did not list AGENT_REGISTRY worker executors) was fixed by adding cli._roles_usage_with_workers() appending the live available_worker_executors() roster to the --help / no-arg / unknown-subcommand teaching paths, plus 2 regression tests (25 total pass). A single codex audit-only at iteration 2 then genuinely SIGNED OFF (2.9M tokens, no blocking findings, one advisory). The iteration-2 placement was deliberate to out-rank the stale i1 needs_changes envelope under closeout._latest_auditor_envelope's highest-iteration selection (the D028 hazard). Finalized via signed_off_finalizer (no-paid flip). Note: codex backend DID recover and deliver a real verdict this time — earlier-session network failures were transient.

title: Skill applicability needs invocation rubrics, not a central router
body: Add F011 to turn advisory applicable-skills output into safe skill recommendations. The rule mirrors the broader one-source-of-truth principle: each SKILL.md declares its own invocation metadata, while DontPanic uses one generic evaluator to classify auto_run, suggest, approval_required, blocked_missing_inputs, or not_applicable. Read-only bounded skills may be auto-run only with complete inputs and allowlisted commands. Mutating, credentialed, networked, paid, external-write, or indefinite-loop skills require approval or are suggested. This prevents humans and interactive agents from spending cycles remembering when to use valuable skills while avoiding blind automation.

title: F011 hardens auto-run with allowlist, precedence, and migration path
body: Review accepted F011's architecture but identified three implementation-critical gaps: the auto-run allowlist must be first-class, risk classification needs deterministic precedence/conflict rules, and existing skills need a lightweight path to gain rubrics. F011 now requires a versioned auditable allowlist surfaced by doctor/reconcile/config inventory, pure evaluator input via SkillInvocationContext, downgrade/block precedence for contradictory unsafe metadata, a never_suggest opt-out, and a rubric suggestion/doctor advisory path for high-value skills missing invocation metadata.

title: Switch to dontpanic --volley harness for all remaining features (F007+); finalize F005/F006
body: Operator directive: stop operator-driven implementation; orchestrate ALL remaining onboarding-v0 work through the dontpanic harness (dispatch_volley: claude implementer + codex auditor) so each feature gets independent cross-agent perspectives rather than a single operator bias. Vindicated by the F005/F006 batched codex audit (evidence/codex-F005-F006-audit-i0.json), which caught a high-severity manifest-validation bug + 3 other findings the operator pass missed; all four fixed at 7d0a2cb and re-green (3090 passed). F005+F006 flipped passes:true (operator-accepted post-audit-fix) to clear the F007 dep-gate. F007 onward dispatch via `dontpanic <plan> --feature FNNN --volley`.

title: Sharpen F007 AC7 (exact_command must be CLI-grammar-validated) after harness stall
body: F007 volley iterated 2 real rounds (cap fix held, codex 63%, no budget trip) and made genuine progress (round-1 wired the dashboard ActionItems codex flagged in round 0), but stopped_no_progress: codex held needs_changes across both rounds on ONE coherent root cause — the implementer emits exact_command strings that are not actually runnable. Cross-agent value confirmed: claude self-signed-off twice while emitting invalid commands; codex caught them by checking against the live CLI. Per operator choice (sharpen + one more volley), AC7 is made concrete: "validated" now means runnable against the live CLI grammar (correct subcommand + required args, no exit-2 usage error) and state-respecting, with 4 enumerated bars 7a–7d (no redispatch when max_iterations exhausted; resume carries --gate/--all; reconcile names homes; referenced dashboard affordance present in the built cache). AC8 extended to require 7a–7d as direct tests. This is AC-clarification (the intent — 'safe and validated' — is unchanged; only the testable bar is concretized), not scope expansion. Re-dispatching one bounded volley (--max-iterations 2). Separately noted for a later harness-improvement pass: stopped_no_progress fired on verdict-equality even though the finding COUNT shrank 5→4 (real progress) — the Design-B count-based carve-out did not save this case because the verdict string was the no-progress key here.

title: Split F007 into F007 (decision engine + exact_command + finalizer) and F007b (live-path completeness)
body: F007 made real progress across 3 dispatches (~7 paid rounds: fixed exact_command bars 7a-7d, wired dashboard ActionItems) but would not converge in autonomous 2-round bursts — the no_progress breaker correctly fired each time because the verdict stayed needs_changes. Triage of the final codex envelope: all 3 remaining findings are REAL (no spec-drift): (#1 high) projects-add re-onboard needs --force --yes [exact_command validity, same class as 7a-7d]; (#2 high) collect_state() surfaces only some setup states to the live what-now/dashboard path — registration/onboarding/roles/doctor/brief guidance is builder-only and unreachable [AC3/AC5 live-path completeness gap]; (#3 med) dashboard ActionItem IDs omit feature_id so distinct features collapse. Root cause: F007 is over-scoped for a 2-round volley (12 ACs x CLI+dashboard parity x ~12 decision states). Per operator choice, SPLIT: F007 keeps the decision engine + ALL exact_command validity (added 7e = projects-add --force --yes) + no-paid finalizer; new F007b (depends_on F007) takes live-path completeness (collect_state surfaces all setup/doctor states, what-now+dashboard parity, ActionItem feature_id uniqueness) = codex findings #2 + #3. Scope/delta: net +1 feature (11->12); no AC dropped — finding #2/#3 relocated, not waived. Volley F007 first (only #1/7e remains in scope -> should converge in 1 round), then F007b, then F008-F010. Chain now F007 -> F007b -> F008 -> {F009,F011} -> F010.

title: F012 NOT closed — operator caught real unaddressed validator defect; sharpen AC6/AC7 + re-volley
body: F012 ran 4 rounds (findings 4->3->2 then a blocked-on-sandbox round where the implementer self-signed-off + 125 local tests green). The ENVIRONMENTAL_BLOCKER breaker correctly flagged codex's pytest FileNotFoundError (auditor sandbox has no usable tempdir) as advisory, recommending operator local verification. Operator ran the suites locally (125 passed) BUT then directly validated the emitted setup commands against command_validation.validate_command_tokens: ALL of agent brief / finalize / what-now / orchestrate / doctor --agent / doctor --project / reconcile homes / projects add --onboard are REJECTED (the validator allowlist is stale, predating F002/F003/F005/F006/F007), and operations_guidance.py STILL emits `doctor --project <name>` (l818) and `projects add ... --onboard` (l753/798) as exact_commands. This is codex's i2 HIGH finding, UNADDRESSED; the 125 green tests miss it because they assert command STRINGS without running the validator (codex i2 MEDIUM finding). So F012 is genuinely incomplete — NOT closed as operator-verified (that would have rubber-stamped a real cross-agent finding). Lesson: signed_off + green tests + environmental-only auditor blocker is NOT sufficient to close when the auditor's prior substantive finding was never verified-resolved; operator must independently confirm the finding is fixed, not just that tests pass. Sharpened F012 AC6 (validator must recognize the full emitted command surface; else advisory) + AC7 (a test must round-trip EVERY emitted exact_command through validate_command_tokens). Re-volleying F012.

title: Split F008 into F008 (inventory core + validated safe_commands) and F013 (dashboard Settings/Setup rendering)
body: F008 stalled stopped_no_progress after 2 rounds (both needs_changes), but findings CHANGED round-to-round (i0: dashboard-not-wired[high] + safe_command-not-validated[med] + weak-tests[med]; i1: invalid-roles-reported-ok[high] + active-hint-not-auto-detected[med] + build/start-rendered-as-edit-affordance[med]) = real progress, and the i1 implementer TIMED OUT at 600s. Same over-scope signature as F007 (12 ACs x CLI+dashboard exceeds a single 600s dispatch). All findings real (no spec-drift). Per the proven F007->F012 pattern, SPLIT: F008 keeps inventory model + providers + CLI + VALIDATED safe_commands (route through validate_command_tokens like F012/D036) + correct status (invalid roles -> non-ok, not ok); new F013 (depends_on F008) takes dashboard Settings/Setup card rendering + active-hint auto-detection + edit-vs-action affordance = codex's dashboard findings. Added F008 AC2b (correct status), AC5b (validated safe_command + no build/start as edit), AC8 round-trip test. Net +1 feature (12->13). No AC dropped. Chain: F008 -> F013 -> {F009,F011} -> F010. Re-volleying F008 core.

title: F008 core: sharpen status-correctness from exemplar to general invariant (AC2c)
body: Post-split F008 core no longer times out (implementer signs off each round) — the split fixed the 600s over-scope. But it still stopped_no_progress because AC2b stated 'correct status' via ONE example (roles not in AGENT_REGISTRY); the implementer fixes the example, codex generalizes to the next provider (i0 capabilities-optimistic, i1 quota-ok-without-calibration + its test gap) = whack-a-mole on an exemplar AC. This is the design-volley lesson in miniature: an exemplar AC invites per-example fixes; the invariant must be stated class-wide with a parametrized test. Sharpened AC2c: non-ok status is a GENERAL invariant across EVERY provider + a single parametrized test asserts it per-provider. Not over-scope (no timeouts) — AC precision. Re-volleying F008 core once more.

title: F008 paused mid-grind (caps hard-stop) — state recorded; pivot to plan-review plan
body: F008 core (post-split, AC2c general-invariant) progressed but did not converge; paused to draft the plan-review capability. STATE AS OF PAUSE: implementer added the parametrized status-invariant test framework but codex i0 (AC2c round) still found 4 real issues: (high) core config providers report ok for present-but-UNLOADABLE files; (high) a TRIPPED circuit breaker still reports ok; (med) the class-wide non-optimistic test uses WEAK cases that miss those invalid states (same testability blind spot as F012 string-equality); (med) SCOPE BLEED — the patch touched dashboard/pages/settings/* which is F013 scope, not F008 (codex caught cross-feature edit at audit time — exactly what a design/pre-dispatch gate would prevent). HARD STOP: the volley stopped_budget not on a real defect but because ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json was reset to {} (invalid: schema_version must be 1) — every dispatch is now blocked until caps is a valid file. Operator reset it intentionally; not re-seeding without direction. RESUME PLAN for F008: (1) per-provider invalid-state status for unloadable-config + tripped-breaker providers; (2) strengthen the parametrized test inputs to actually exercise each invalid state; (3) revert the F013 dashboard bleed (belongs to F013). Also: the {} caps hard-stop is itself a product gap — DontPanic should surface invalid config with actionable remediation, not a low-level schema crash (captured as a feature in the new plan-review plan). Onboarding-v0 status unchanged: F005/F006/F007/F012 done+committed (5660b5c); F008/F013/F009/F011/F010 remain.

title: F008 resume: caps reseeded (init), F013 bleed reverted, AC2d tight-scope added
body: Resuming F008 after the plan-review draft. Caps reseeded deliberately via `quota-caps init` (schema_version:1; codex.plus.rolling_5h=48987969 = 1.25x observed 39.19M) — init baseline, not a habitual large override per operator pref; a higher codex cap later is a fresh recorded decision. Reverted the F013 dashboard/settings bleed from the worktree (dashboard/core.js, dashboard/pages/settings/*, settings-inventory-logic.js, settings-inventory-page.test.js, and the extra dashboard.py edits) back to committed HEAD 5660b5c, keeping F008's own config_inventory.py + test + cli `config inventory`. Added AC2d hard close-out scope to F008: (a) NO dashboard/* edits (F013 scope) or the AC fails; (b) unloadable-config provider non-ok; (c) tripped-breaker provider non-ok; (d) the parametrized invariant test must use REAL invalid-state inputs that fail-before/pass-after, not weak cases. Re-dispatching F008 with these as hard auditor checks.

body: Deliberate codex-cap decision (operator-approved). dispatch readiness requires the codex rolling_7d window, which `quota-caps init` does not seed (only 5h). Added codex.plus.rolling_7d cap=975000000 (1.25x observed 780410457, matching init's 1.25x derivation method) so onboarding-v0 F008 can dispatch. Reason recorded per operator policy that codex cap additions are explicit decisions, not habitual overrides. The circular init->config_required friction itself is captured as plan-review F009 evidence (D002 in 2026-06-01-001).

title: Operator decision: raise codex rolling_5h cap to 2e8 (proxy non-functional) — durable for dogfood
body: Operator-approved. F008 tight-scope round ran clean (no F013 bleed; ~1 finding from done: environments provider optimistic-status + its real-input test) but died stopped_budget: codex 5h breaker read 1.264e8 > init cap 48987969. Diagnosis conclusive: codex tokens_local_proxy 5h is uncalibrated/non-functional — ~0 at rest (direct probe) vs constant 1.264e8 in-volley (breaker) — so any init-derived cap always false-trips in-volley. Raised codex.plus.rolling_5h to 2e8 (above 1.264e8), durable for the remaining onboarding-v0 chain (F008/F013/F009/F011/F010) to stop re-hitting this. This effectively disables the codex 5h spend-guard until fixed; real fix tracked as plan-review 2026-06-01-001 F009 (+ a quota calibration feature). Not a habitual override — a recorded, scoped decision per operator policy (cf D041 for the 7d window).

Residual: init derives codex 5h cap from at-rest proxy (~45M) but breaker reads stuck ~1.264e8 (readiness codex=226%), so dispatch still trips the in-loop 5h breaker. title: F008 quota-unblocked but still wide: non-optimistic-status invariant spans ~16 providers (per-provider grind)
body: With quota fixed (F009 + D044 cap) F008 finally ran 2 clean volleys, no quota crash, tight scope held (no dashboard bleed). But still stopped_no_progress: codex keeps surfacing the NEXT provider that reports ok on an invalid state (run findings: --project invalid fallback; quota-state provider missing; global_config non-runnable worker defaults) plus a too-narrow invariant test. Root: AC2c's 'every provider reports non-ok on invalid state' spans ~16 providers and is being satisfied reactively one-per-round, so it never reaches zero in a 2-round burst. This is the SAME over-scope signature the plan-review lint is meant to catch: the convergent unit is a SHARED status-derivation helper applied uniformly to all providers + ONE exhaustive parametrized test (every provider x its invalid state), not per-provider patches. Recommended: either (a) re-volley F008 with AC sharpened to require the shared-helper + exhaustive-test approach (so the implementer fixes the whole class at once), (b) split the status-invariant into its own narrow slice, or (c) finish operator-style. Quota is no longer the blocker; F008 sizing is. Latest implementer WIP is in the worktree (uncommitted since 372a8b9).

title: F008 AC2e: require ONE shared status helper + ONE exhaustive per-provider test (whole-class fix)
body: Per operator choice, sharpen F008 to force the convergent unit instead of per-provider whack-a-mole: a single shared status-derivation helper used by every provider + one exhaustive parametrized test enumerating each provider's invalid state (unloadable config, tripped breaker, quota caps-without-calibration, quota-state missing, global_config non-runnable defaults, unsupported roles, invalid manifest, stale onboarding), plus --project-unresolved -> non-ok (no silent machine-only fallback). Same sharpen-the-AC move that converged F007/F012. Re-volleying F008 once.

title: F008 shared-helper landed (AC2e met structurally); F009 v2-loader change LOST/not durable; quota works via v1 file + D044
body: Run8 (AC2e) outcome: the implementer BUILT the shared status helper config_inventory.derive_status(StatusFacts) (config_inventory.py:319) with a by-construction class-wide non-optimistic invariant (comment 291-296) — the expensive over-scope/whack-a-mole problem is SOLVED. Residual is a narrow 3-item punch list (all real, all small): [high] _anthropic_auth_configured() treats is_available() (binary on PATH) as auth -> still optimistic; [medium] inventory emits `dontpanic roles set <role> <executor>` but command_validation doesn't recognize it (F012-class validator gap, again); [low] F008 test files not ruff-clean. F008 NOT closed (op checklist #3 auth-optimism + ruff fail). AC2d clean — no dashboard/settings bleed. CRITICAL handoff fact: the operator-style F009 change to quota_caps_loader.py (accept schema_version:2 + vendors{} + both-window init) is NOT present in the canonical module — load() still validate()s and REJECTS v2 ('schema_version must be 1' / 'unknown vendor key: vendors'). It was lost, most likely reverted when run8's execution env reset the working tree over the uncommitted edit. Nothing references the missing code (cli.py vendors refs are quota_state.json, unrelated), so the tree is consistent. Operational quota works ONLY because ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json is a hand-set valid schema_version:1 file with codex 5h=2e8 (D044) + 7d=982M. NEXT SESSION: do NOT rely on v2 caps loading; F009-as-feature must be re-implemented (re-apply v2 accept + both-window init + the init-samples-breaker-reading extension) and committed before relying on it. F008 next: fix the 3 punch-list items (anthropic auth = real login check not PATH; add `roles set` to command_validation; ruff --fix), add `## Return Condition` h2 to closeout-memo (D004 mechanical gate that skipped signoff_writer), then finalize.
